text:
Maya: FYI handing off to the night shift. Quick summary of the last 6h: we saw repeated KV-cache throttles causing 429s on the text-generation path. Root cause appears to be transient hot-shard pressure after a large batched job from a partner. Impact: some Dedicated customers saw a ~2-4s tail latency increase and occasional 429s; hosted fallbacks kept the majority of traffic alive. We paged at 11:04 UTC and ran mitigations; incident is no longer paged but still under watch. https://redwood.internal/incidents/4321 :eyes:

Maya: Current status
- Mitigation applied: temporary autoscale +2 nodes on pool-gpu-1 (effective 11:18 UTC)
- KV prefix caching warmed for hot keys (partial)
- Request fallback policy enabled to model-variant-b when qps>threshold
- Alert conditions adjusted to avoid noise (see incident log)

Maya: Who's primary/secondary for the night? I'm assigning @Jacob as primary and @Tessa as secondary. Priya, can you cover the 02:00-03:00 UTC gap? There's currently no rotation there.

Jacob: taking primary. thx. I'll keep an eye on queue depth and the 429 rate.

Tessa: secondary, will be reachable by phone. please ping if anything spikes.

Priya: I can pick up 02:00-03:00 UTC. Will add to rotation calendar.

Maya: Thanks. Coverage gap resolved.

Jacob: quick Q — runbook for cache pressure, where live?

Maya: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-pressure
Main checks I use:
```
# check pool-level queue depth
kubectl -n inference exec deploy/queue-watcher -- curl -s http://localhost:9000/metrics | grep queue_depth
# check pod errors
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=runtime -o wide
kubectl -n inference logs deploy/runtime -c runtime --tail=200 | grep -i "throttle"
```
If queue_depth > 200 for >5m escalate and switch routing to fallback pool: see step 4 of runbook.

Sam: small note — autoscaler bumped minNodes from 6 -> 8 as short-term mitig. If we see sustained traffic we'll need to scale to 10 and evaluate model batching config.

deploy-bot: autoscaler: pool-gpu-1 minNodes set to 8 by Sam at 2026-03-21T11:18:12Z

incident-bot: Incident #4321 severity: high -> monitoring. All pages closed at 2026-03-21T11:40:03Z. Postmortem assigned: @Maya (owner), due EOD +2.

Tessa: Do we need to notify any customers directly? I can draft a short note for affected Dedicated customers.

Maya: Yes please. short template: "We observed intermittent latency and rate limits on inference requests due to cache shard pressure between 10:50-11:25 UTC. We applied autoscaling and routing fallbacks; services are stable now. We're following up with a postmortem and mitigation plan."

Tessa: I'll send that to account-team and cc eng-sre.

Priya: Leaving a pointer: check realtime metric dashboard -> infra.kv.cache.pool-gpu-1.queue_depth and alerts -> kv-cache-high-queue. I also added a temporary threshold at 180 to reduce alert noise.

Jacob: Night checklist for whoever is primary: 
1) verify queue_depth < 100 for 15m
2) confirm no new 5xx/429 spikes in logs
3) if spike, run fallback routing: `curl -X POST https://control-plane/internal/reroute -d '{"pool":"fallback","ratio":0.3}'`
4) if reroute doesn't reduce errors in 10m, escalate to SRE pager

Maya: leaving next steps:
- Jacob / Tessa: monitor through the night, escalate if >10% error rate for 10m
- Sam: follow up tomorrow morning to analyze batching and autoscale thresholds
- Maya: start postmortem draft (will include request ids and timeline)

Jacob: ack. I'll run a quick health-check script every hour.

Sam: FYI I opened a ticket to evaluate KV sharding heuristics: INF-8821. Will sync with runtime team tomorrow.

Tessa: Thanks all. I tagged incident channel and added :thumbsup:

Maya: handing off complete. ping me if anything urgent.

incident-bot: Note: postmortem INF-4321 created and assigned to Maya.

Jacob: good handoff. leaving a small note in rotation: remove non-essential batch jobs from 10:30-12:30 UTC windows to avoid rebuilds triggering hot keys.

Priya: done — calendar updated and ops-runbook note added.

Maya: end of thread.
